before.title: Localization of a continuous function by axis-parallel cube integrals
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the Lebesgue-measure interface used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $g:U\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Suppose that $\int_Qg\,d\lambda_n=0$ for every closed axis-parallel cube $Q=\prod_{i<n}[a_i,a_i+\ell]$ with $\ell>0$ and $Q\subseteq U$, the integral being that of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. Then $g=0$ on $U$. In particular, for $n=2$, a continuous function on an open subset of the plane whose integral over every closed axis-parallel square contained in its domain vanishes is identically zero. The hypothesis requires all such cubes with every centre and every side length; a single cube or the cubes through one point do not suffice.
before.strategy: The Countable Choice convention is the Lebesgue interface of [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]] and [[def-countable-choice]]. Suppose $g(p)\ne0$ for some $p\in U$; replacing $g$ by $-g$ if necessary, assume $g(p)>0$. By continuity at $p$ ([[def-metric-continuity]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]) choose $\delta>0$ with $B(p,\delta)\subseteq U$ and $g(x)>g(p)/2$ whenever $d(x,p)<\delta$. The closed cube $Q:=p+[-\delta/(2\sqrt n),\delta/(2\sqrt n)]^n$ satisfies $Q\subseteq B(p,\delta)$, has side length $\ell=\delta/\sqrt n>0$ and satisfies $g\ge g(p)/2$ on $Q$. By [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], $\lambda_n(Q)=(2\delta/(2\sqrt n))^n=\ell^n>0$; the continuous $g$ is Borel measurable ([[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]) and bounded on the compact cube $Q$ ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]]), so the signed integral over $Q$ is defined ([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). Monotonicity and the scalar rules ([[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) give $\int_Qg\ge\int_Q(g(p)/2)\,d\lambda_n=(g(p)/2)\lambda_n(Q)>0$, contradicting the hypothesis $\int_Qg=0$. Hence $g(p)=0$ for every $p\in U$. The planar clause is the case $n=2$. No regularity beyond continuity, and no choice beyond $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is used.

after.title: Surface densities with vanishing test pairings vanish
after.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the surface-measure interface cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $S\subset\Omega$ be a compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface in the sense of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], and let $a:S\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. If $\int_Sa\psi\,dS=0$ for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]), then $a=0$ on $S$. Equivalently, if two continuous densities on $S$ pair equally against every test function, they are equal pointwise on $S$. The conclusion is pointwise and uses the continuity of $a$; a merely locally integrable density would satisfy only an almost-everywhere conclusion, which this statement does not claim.
after.strategy: Assume the stated Countable Choice convention. If $a(x_0)\ne0$, replace $a$ by $-a$ if needed and put $m=a(x_0)/2>0$. Continuity of $a$ on $S$ gives an ambient neighbourhood $N$ of $x_0$ on which $a\ge m$ on $S\cap N$. By the embedded $C^2$ hypothesis, the inverse/implicit-function suppliers give, after permuting coordinates, a graph chart $X(u)=(u,g(u))$ on an open $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ with $X(u_0)=x_0$ and $g\in C^2(D)$. Choose an open ambient chart neighbourhood $O\subset\Omega\cap N$ containing $x_0$, meeting $S$ only in this graph chart. Choose $0<r<R$ with $\overline B_R(x_0)\subset O$. The actual ambient bump supplied by [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]] is a function $\psi\in C_c^\infty(B_R(x_0))$, $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(x_0)$; extended by zero it is in $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ by [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]. There is no product-extension assertion for arbitrary planar tests. By continuity of $X$, choose a closed nondegenerate parameter square $C\subset D$ around $u_0$ with $X(C)\subset B_r(x_0)$. The graph density is $J_X=\sqrt{1+|\nabla g|^2}\ge1$ by [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]. The surface measure and restriction to Borel chart subsets are exactly those of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]; chart independence lets the integral of a function supported in $S\cap O$ be computed in this chart. Equivalently one may choose a compact Jordan region $C'\Subset D$, obtained as a finite union of closed parameter squares lying in $D$ and covering the compact parameter preimage of its support and use [[thm-surface-integrals-over-c-one-graphs]] followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] for the continuous graph integrand on $C'$. On the support of $\psi|_S$ we have $a\ge m$, and $\psi=1$ on $X(C)$. Consequently monotonicity gives $\int_S a\psi\,dS\ge m\int_{X(C)}1\,dS=m\int_C J_X\,d\lambda_2\ge m\lambda_2(C)>0$; [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]] gives $\lambda_2(C)=\ell^2>0$. This contradicts the given zero pairing. Every $x_0\in S$ therefore has $a(x_0)=0$, and applying this to the difference proves the equal-density clause. The compact embedded $C^2$ interface here is within the published compact embedded $C^1$ surface-measure class, with no change to its measure convention; in particular the closed stationary interfaces used by the jump theorem are covered. No new Choice principle is used. The empty-surface case is immediate.

before.title: Fixed volume and patch test geometries, outward normals and induced orientations
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention already carried by the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentations and by the compact $C^1$ surface measure cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ open and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ a nonempty open interval. This definition fixes the time-independent spatial test geometries of the integral form of the Maxwell equations.

(a) [Volume test geometry] A volume test geometry in $\Omega$ is a pair $(V,\nu_V)$ where $V\subseteq\Omega$ is a nonempty bounded open set with a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of its boundary ([[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]) and $\nu_V$ is the outward unit normal of that presentation off its edge set ([[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]). The closed-surface flux of a field $F$ continuous on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$ is the finite face sum
$$\oint_{\partial V}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS:=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS,$$
with the face surface integrals of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. Every axis-parallel closed box $V=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]$ with $a_i<b_i$ and $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$ carries its natural six-face presentation, whose faces are its two-dimensional faces with the outward normals $\pm e_i$; it is therefore a volume test geometry.

(b) [Patch test geometry] A patch test geometry in $\Omega$ is a regular $C^2$ surface patch $(D,r)$ over a finite elementary Green region in the sense of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]], [[def-admissible-regular-parametrized-surface-patch]]): $D\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ is a finite elementary Green region, $r$ is of class $C^2$ on an open neighbourhood of $D$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), $r_u\times r_v\ne0$ on the interior of $D$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) and no interior parameter point shares its image with a distinct point of $D$. Its induced boundary chain $\partial S=r(\partial D)$ and its circulation $\oint_{\partial S}F\cdot d\mathbf r$ for a field continuous on the image are those of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]); its oriented flux of a field $F$ continuous on the image is
$$\int_SF\cdot n_S\,dS:=\int_D(F\circ r)\cdot(r_u\times r_v)\,dudv,$$
the scalar Riemann integral of the continuous integrand on the compact Jordan parameter region, in the orientation induced by $r$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). The pair $(D,r)$ is part of the data. Every affine graph patch $r(u,v)=(u,v,\varphi(u,v))$ over an axis-parallel square $D=[c_1,c_1+\ell]\times[c_2,c_2+\ell]$ with $\ell>0$, whose graph lies in $\Omega$ with $\varphi$ affine (for instance constant), and more generally every affine regular patch over such a square, is a patch test geometry: the square is a finite elementary Green region, and $r$ is smooth and regular with $\varphi_u,\varphi_v$ constant.

(c) [Regularity convention] When an integral identity of this framework is asserted for a volume test geometry $V$, respectively for a patch test geometry $S$, with respect to a field $F$ of stated class $C^k$, it concerns fields defined and of class $C^k$ on an open neighbourhood of $\overline V$ in $\Omega$, respectively of the image $r[D]$ in $\Omega$; when the identity involves a time derivative of a flux, the field is defined with the stated regularity on a neighbourhood of that compact set times the compact time interval of the assertion. No regularity away from these neighbourhoods is asserted.

(d) [Conventions and scope] Test geometries are fixed spatial subsets of $\Omega$ and carry no motion. A patch's orientation is the one induced by its parametrization, and its induced boundary chain has the compatible orientation of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]], so that the classical Stokes theorem applies with a plus sign. The definition retains the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of the imported boundary and surface-measure definitions; it asserts no differential equation, no physical law and no existence of fields.
before.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition. Clause (a) composes the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation with its outward normal and the compact-hypersurface face integral; the box is verified as an instance by listing its six faces (each a compact subset of a regular $C^1$ hypersurface patch, namely a coordinate plane), its twelve edges and eight vertices as the edge set, and noting that the face-edge intersections have surface measure zero and that outside the edges the boundary is locally a coordinate $C^1$ graph with the box on one side. Clause (b) composes the $C^2$ patch over a finite elementary Green region with the induced boundary chain and the oriented patch flux; an affine graph over an axis-parallel square is verified as an instance because a rectangle is both a type $I$ and a type $II$ region with the natural elementary decomposition, so the square carries a finite elementary Green presentation. Clause (c) is a regularity convention recording that all integral identities of this page quantify over fields on neighbourhoods of the compact test sets, which is exactly the hypothesis class of the imported divergence and Stokes theorems. Clause (d) records the orientation and countability conventions and states explicitly that the definition introduces no physical law. Nothing here asserts that every bounded domain is admissible, that a disc is a legal parameter region, or that a physical test geometry is realised by an apparatus.

before.title: Smooth differential-integral equivalence for every admissible test geometry
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the imported piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure definitions ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $E,B$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ source fields of [[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$; and let $(V,\nu_V)$ and $(D,r)$ be the volume and patch test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]. Assume the fields are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ and that the additional derivatives appearing below exist and are continuous there; for instance $E,B$ jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ is sufficient.

(a) [Differential implies integral] If the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, then for every volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and every $t\in I$,
$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \oint_{\partial V}B(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=0,$$
and for every patch test geometry $(D,r)$ the flux functions $t\mapsto\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and $t\mapsto\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ are differentiable on $I$ and, for every $t\in I$,
$$\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=-\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS,\qquad \oint_{\partial S}B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\mu_0\int_SJ(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS+c^{-2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS.$$

(b) [Integral implies differential] Conversely, suppose the two volume identities of (a) hold for every volume test geometry and every $t\in I$, and that for every patch test geometry the two flux functions are differentiable on $I$ and the two patch identities of (a) hold for every $t\in I$. Then the four smooth-branch equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold pointwise on $\Omega\times I$:
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

The equivalence is asserted for the exact class of test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], which contains the axis-parallel boxes and the affine square patches; it is not a recovery from one selected volume or one selected patch, and the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the time derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] are the operators used.

before.title: Stationary-sheet jump conditions of the weak Maxwell equations
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the interface and surface-measure definitions cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and source fields of [[def-em-sources]].

Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density). Let $E,B$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with one-sided $C^1$ traces on $S$ at every $t\in I$, and let $\rho_v,J_v$ be continuous on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces of such a field $F$.

Suppose that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair
$$\rho=\rho_v+\rho_S,\qquad J=J_v+J_S,$$
where $(\rho_S,J_S)$ is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with densities $\sigma,K$ and the pairings there, in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e), and where the volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Then, pointwise on $S\times I$,
$$n\cdot[E]=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad n\times[B]=\mu_0K,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,$$
with the ordinary Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Equivalently, the surface current density is $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}\,n\times[B]$ and the surface charge density is $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot[E]$.

The theorem assumes a stationary interface: the hypersurface $S$ and its normal do not depend on $t$, so the one-sided $C^1$ traces also make $\partial_tE$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally integrable, contributing no delta terms. No magnetic surface charge or magnetic surface current is present in the sources, and correspondingly the last two identities assert the absence of magnetic sheet delta terms. A moving interface, a normal sheet current, or a sheet whose support changes with time is outside this statement and would require additional terms.
before.strategy:
Assume the fields of the statement. Because $S$ is stationary, the interface formula of [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] applies to the spatial divergence and curl of each field at each time, with the same normal convention $n$ from $\Omega_-$ to $\Omega_+$ and jump $[F]=F_+-F_-$ as fixed in [[def-em-surface-distribution]] and [[def-em-weak-sources]](c); in particular
$$\operatorname{div}E=\{\operatorname{div}E\}+n\cdot[E]\,\delta_{S\times I},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\{\operatorname{curl}B\}+n\times[B]\,\delta_{S\times I}$$
as distributions on $U$, where $\{\ \}$ denotes the locally integrable function equal to the classical divergence or curl on each open side, and $\delta_{S\times I}$ is the functional $\psi\mapsto\int_I\int_S\psi\,dS\,dt$ built from the sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c).

First separate the ordinary from the singular parts. Restrict the pairing of the weak Gauss law $\operatorname{div}E=\rho_v/\varepsilon_0+\rho_S/\varepsilon_0$ to test functions supported in $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$: the singular term vanishes, so $\int_{(\Omega\setminus S)\times I}(\{\operatorname{div}E\}-\rho_v/\varepsilon_0)\psi=0$ for every such test function. The function $g:=\{\operatorname{div}E\}-\rho_v/\varepsilon_0$ is continuous on the open set $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and its integral against every test function supported there vanishes; such a continuous $g$ vanishes identically, because if $g(p)\ne0$ one chooses a ball around $p$ on which $g$ has one sign with $|g|\ge|g(p)|/2$ and a nonnegative bump supported in it with positive integral ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]), contradicting the vanishing by [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] and [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]. Hence $\{\operatorname{div}E\}=\rho_v/\varepsilon_0$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$, and subtracting the resulting identity from the weak equation leaves
$$(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0)\,\delta_{S\times I}=0.$$
Testing with $\psi(x,t)=\varphi(x)\eta(t)$, $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$, and using that the inner integral is continuous in $t$ gives $\int_I\eta(t)\int_S\bigl(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0\bigr)\varphi\,dS\,dt=0$ for all $\eta$; the function $F(t):=\int_S(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0)\varphi\,dS$ is continuous on $I$, and a continuous function on an interval whose integral against every compactly supported test vanishes is identically zero, by the same one-dimensional sign-and-bump argument ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]); hence $F(t)=0$ for every $t\in I$, that is, $\int_S(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0)\varphi\,dS=0$ at every $t\in I$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); the surface density $n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ is continuous on the compact $S$ at each such $t$, so [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] gives $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ pointwise on $S\times I$. Repeating the same two-step argument — off-sheet vanishing by the sign-and-bump localization, then surface localization — with the other three weak equations:
- from $\operatorname{div}B=0$ (no volume magnetic source and no magnetic sheet term): $n\cdot[B]=0$ on $S\times I$;
- from $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$, whose right side is represented by the locally integrable function $-\partial_tB$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with no delta part because the interface is stationary and $B$ has one-sided $C^1$ traces: $n\times[E]=0$ on $S\times I$;
- from $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J_v+c^{-2}\partial_tE+\mu_0J_S$, where $J_S$ is the sheet functional with density $K$: $n\times[B]=\mu_0K$ on $S\times I$, which is exactly $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}n\times[B]$ since $n\times[B]$ is tangential.
All hypotheses used are those stated: the one-sided $C^1$ traces make the interface formula applicable ([[lem-em-interface-derivatives]]), continuity of $\rho_v,J_v$ on the open complement makes the sign-and-bump localization applicable there, and continuity of the traces and of $\sigma,K$ makes [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] applicable. The marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the convention of the interface and surface-measure items; no further choice is used.

after.title: Stationary-sheet jump conditions of the weak Maxwell equations
after.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the interface and surface-measure definitions cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and source fields of [[def-em-sources]].

Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density). Let $E,B$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with the following explicit joint one-sided regularity: around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. Thus the fields and their first space/time derivatives extend continuously to that side of $S\times I$, locally uniformly on compact cylinders, and let $\rho_v,J_v$ be continuous on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces of such a field $F$.

Suppose that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair
$$\rho=\rho_v+\rho_S,\qquad J=J_v+J_S,$$
where $(\rho_S,J_S)$ is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with densities $\sigma,K$ and the pairings there, in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e), and where the volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Then, pointwise on $S\times I$,
$$n\cdot[E]=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad n\times[B]=\mu_0K,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,$$
with the ordinary Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Equivalently, the surface current density is $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}\,n\times[B]$ and the surface charge density is $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot[E]$.

The theorem assumes a stationary interface: the hypersurface $S$ and its normal do not depend on $t$, so the one-sided $C^1$ traces also make $\partial_tE$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally integrable, contributing no delta terms. No magnetic surface charge or magnetic surface current is present in the sources, and correspondingly the last two identities assert the absence of magnetic sheet delta terms. A moving interface, a normal sheet current, or a sheet whose support changes with time is outside this statement and would require additional terms.

[General weak trace branch] The weak Maxwell framework continues to allow the full locally integrable field/source class, without asserting undefined classical trace values. If instead of the joint extension condition the fields have the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time, assume in addition that their piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega\times I)$ and that their one-sided field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ with respect to $dS\,dt$. Then the same four jump identities hold as equalities of sheet distributions and for $dS\,dt$-almost every $(x,t)$; since the traces are spatially continuous at each fixed time, they hold for every $x\in S$ for almost every $t\in I$. They hold at every $(x,t)$ whenever the jump densities are additionally jointly continuous. Merely having one-sided spatial $C^1$ traces separately at every time does not justify this last upgrade.
after.strategy:
First justify the spacetime use of the spatial supplier. For a compactly supported spacetime test $\psi$, let $K\subset\Omega$ be its compact spatial support projection and let $L\Subset I$ be a compact interval containing its time support. Choose finitely many spatial stationary graph neighbourhoods and interior open sets covering $K$. [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]] gives smooth nonnegative spatial functions $\phi_j$ compactly supported in those sets with $\sum_j\phi_j=1$ near $K$. Explicitly, first choose finitely many nonnegative ambient bumps $\chi_j$ subordinate to that cover whose sum $s$ is positive near $K$; a cutoff $\theta\in C_c^\infty(\{s>0\})$ equal to one near $K$ exists by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]], and $\phi_j=\theta\chi_j/s$ on $\{s>0\}$, extended by zero elsewhere, is smooth since $\operatorname{supp}\theta$ stays compactly inside the positive set. Their sum is $\theta=1$ near $K$, so $\psi=\sum_j\phi_j\psi$. This partition is independent of time, hence $\partial_t(\phi_j\psi)=\phi_j\partial_t\psi$ and temporal integration by parts acquires no partition derivative. On each spatial chart times $L$, the local joint one-sided extensions have a finite subcover of the relevant compact sheet-time subset, giving the compact bounds used below; interior compact supports are already covered by the ordinary joint $C^1$ assumption. In the joint branch the one-sided $C^1$ extensions and their derivatives are bounded on each compact closed half-cylinder, so the piecewise derivatives are locally integrable and the jumps are jointly continuous and bounded there. Apply [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] to each component of the spatial slice at every fixed $t$ and integrate in $t$. The terms $F\partial_i\psi$, $(\partial_i F)\psi$ and $n_i[F]\psi$ are absolutely integrable on the compact support (the last uses the finite compact surface measure of [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]), so [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] justifies integrating the identity. This gives $\partial_iF_j=\{\partial_iF_j\}+n_i[F_j]\delta_{S\times I}$, and contraction/antisymmetrization gives the divergence/curl formulas. For the temporal derivative, on each fixed spatial side, [[thm-integration-by-parts]] on a compact time interval containing the test support, followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], gives $-\int F_j\partial_t\psi=\int (\partial_tF_j)\psi$, with no endpoint term since the test support is compact in $I$. Integrate in $x$ by the same Fubini theorem. The sides are stationary, so no derivative of a moving spatial indicator occurs and $\partial_tF_j=\{\partial_tF_j\}$ with no sheet term.

The spatial sheet $S$ has three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero: in each finite graph chart every normal section is a singleton, so Fubini gives zero volume, and the coordinate permutation preserves Lebesgue measure. Consequently $S\times I$ is locally four-dimensional null. Restrict each weak Maxwell identity to tests away from $S\times I$. The resulting ordinary residuals are continuous on the open complement, so the existing sign-and-ambient-bump argument forces them to vanish pointwise there. The ordinary residuals are locally integrable and differ from zero only on the null sheet, hence represent zero regular distributions by [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]. Subtract them to obtain the four sheet identities with densities $n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\cdot[B]$, $n\times[E]$, $n\times[B]-\mu_0K$. For every spatial $\varphi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, each scalar component $H(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$ is continuous: on a compact time interval, joint continuity on the compact sheet gives uniform convergence as $t\to t_0$, and the bound $|H(t)-H(t_0)|\le S(S)\|\varphi\|_\infty\sup_{x\in S}|a(x,t)-a(x,t_0)|$ tends to zero. Testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ and using the one-dimensional sign-and-bump argument shows $H(t)=0$ at every time. Apply [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] at that time and componentwise to get the four pointwise jumps. Tangentiality of $n\times[B]$ gives the stated current formula.

For the general weak trace branch, the additional local $L^1$ hypotheses on piecewise derivatives and traces justify the same Fubini arguments without compact uniform bounds. Temporal integration by parts is valid first on compact subintervals for each fixed off-sheet $x$, since the field is $C^1$ there; its integrable derivative and the test's compact support justify the integrated identity. The sheet residuals are therefore zero as distributions. For each fixed ambient spatial test $\varphi$, Fubini gives the locally integrable time function $H_\varphi(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$, and testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ shows its regular distribution is zero. The one-dimensional case of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] gives $H_\varphi(t)=0$ for almost every time. To obtain one exceptional time set, use the countable explicit ambient bumps with rational centres $q\in\mathbb Q^3$ and rational radii $0<r<R$ for which $\overline B_R(q)\subset\Omega$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(q)$ and supported in $B_R(q)$. They are defined by the fixed smooth-step formula in [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], so no arbitrary choice of a test for each triple is needed. Remove the countable union of the null time sets for these tests, which remains null by [[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]. For a remaining time, a nonzero continuous spatial residual at any $x_0\in S$ has one strict sign on a sufficiently small graph neighbourhood. Density of the rationals ([[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]) gives one of those ambient balls wholly inside that neighbourhood whose inner ball contains $x_0$. A positive-area graph cell in its inner ball, as in [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]], makes its pairing nonzero, contradiction. Thus each residual vanishes at every spatial point for almost every time, which also proves the sheet-a.e. assertion. Joint continuity, if separately assumed, similarly upgrades to all times using positive-area cells times nondegenerate time intervals. The counterexample recorded in this proposal proves why this qualification cannot be omitted. All four electromagnetic conclusions and the unrestricted weak Maxwell framework are retained at their strongest justified regularity level; no Sobolev trace theorem or undeclared Choice principle is used.
